g.passage: There are some people who habitually, and from a strong sense of duty, live on the shady side of life. Metaphorically speaking, the sunshine may almost touch the very path on which they are treading, but they shrink from and avoid it, having a strong preference for the shade, but considering themselves martyrs while they live in it. Mrs. Cameron was one of these people. The circumstances of her life had elected plenty of sunshine for her; she had a devoted and excellent husband, an abundant income, and admirable health. It is true she had no children, and it is also true that she had brought herself by careful cultivation to a state of chronic ill-temper.

options: It describes Mrs. Cameron's poor health and then explains how her husband came to cure her.
It states a general claim about certain people and then gives Mrs. Cameron as an example.
It contrasts two married couples and then judges which of the two is the happier pair.
It recounts a sunny walk in the country and then shifts to a memory of a darker period.
g.explanation: 지문은 '삶의 그늘진 쪽에 사는 사람들'에 대한 일반적 진술로 시작한다. 이어 'Mrs. Cameron was one of these people'이라는 문장으로 구체적 사례를 제시하고 그녀의 환경을 덧붙인다. 그러므로 B가 정답이다. 그녀는 건강이 좋다고 했으므로 A는 틀리고, C·D의 비교나 산책 장면은 없다.

g.passage:
The chamber of the solitary student is peopled with immortal guests. He has friends who are always steadfast, who are never false, who are silent when he is weary, who go forth with him to his work, who await his return. In the literature of the world a grand society is open to all who choose to enter it.

Books are the chief food of our intellectual life.--There are men that have, indeed, done great things who have read but little. These have had their want of mental training compensated by their powers of observation and experience of life. But they have been for the most part exceptional men, and it is possible they might have done better if they had studied more.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It tells the story of one solitary student and then describes the friends he has lost.
It lists several famous books and then ranks them by their value to young scholars.
It praises books as companions and then answers an objection about light readers.
It argues against heavy reading and then admits that books can offer some comfort.
g.explanation: 첫 단락은 책을 '불멸의 손님'이자 변치 않는 친구로 비유하며 찬양한다. 둘째 단락은 적게 읽고도 큰일을 한 사람들이 있다는 반론을 들고, 그들은 예외였으며 더 공부했다면 나았을 것이라고 답한다. 따라서 C가 구조를 정확히 요약한다. A의 잃어버린 친구, B의 책 순위, D의 독서 반대는 지문과 맞지 않는다.

I was, however, happily disappointed, when at the close of the ceremony the company retired, and my sisters went about employing every means for my consolation and comfort.

Being now settled and provided with a home, I was employed in nursing the children, and doing light work about the house. Occasionally I was sent out with the Indian hunters, when they went but a short distance, to help them carry their game.

My situation was easy; I had no particular hardships to endure. But still, the recollection of my parents, my brothers and sisters, my home, and my own captivity, destroyed my happiness, and made me constantly solitary, lonesome and gloomy.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It lists the narrator's daily chores and then explains how she escaped from captivity.
It describes a harsh punishment and then the narrator's secret plan to seek revenge.
It praises the hunters' great skill and then describes one hunt the narrator joined.
It describes the narrator's easy new routine and then reveals her lasting sorrow.
g.explanation: 지문은 의식이 끝난 뒤 자매들의 위로와 아이 돌보기·가벼운 일로 이루어진 새 생활을 설명한다. 이어 'My situation was easy'라고 말한 뒤 'But still'로 전환하며 가족에 대한 기억이 행복을 앗아 갔다고 밝힌다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. 탈출·복수·사냥 찬양은 지문에 없으므로 A, B, C는 틀리다.

g.passage:
With a firm step he walked from his prison to the foot of the gibbet, and mounted the steps. Resting a moment, he addressed the spectators, exhorting them to take example from his dreadful fate, and to avoid the evil courses which had, step by step, conducted him to it. At length the executioner warned him that his time was up.

"I am ready," he answered, and was about to submit his neck to the fatal noose, when, starting back, he exclaimed in a voice of agony, "He is come! he is come! Oh, save me from him!--save me!"

Before he could utter more, the drop was let fall, and all was soon over. The rest of the crew died making no sign.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: Detached, reporting the man's last moments without comment
Admiring, praising the man as a hero who faces death bravely
Mocking, treating the man's cry of terror as a source of humor
Outraged, protesting that the execution is unjust and cruel
g.explanation: 서술자는 사형수가 교수대에 오르고 군중에게 훈계하는 과정을 감정 표현 없이 차례로 전한다. 그의 절규 뒤에도 'all was soon over', 'The rest of the crew died making no sign'처럼 짧고 담담하게 마무리한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. 영웅으로 찬양하거나 조롱하거나 처형에 분노하는 표현은 없으므로 B, C, D는 틀리다.

g.passage:
Perhaps I was wrong in this: I dare say I was, as I nearly always am. It is the people who make the greatest demands that get the largest supplies. But it was not in me either to make the one or to claim the other; and we can only act according to our kind.

In looking back on past events I once used to think: "How much better things would have turned out, if only I had acted differently." But as I grew older and wiser I changed the formula to: "How much better things would have turned out, if only I had had the power to act differently." And at the back of my mind I knew that I never had had the power.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: Bitter, blaming other people for making unfair demands on the narrator
Resigned, accepting that the narrator lacked power to act otherwise
Proud, confident that the narrator's past choices were always correct
Hopeful, expecting that the narrator will act more boldly in the future
g.explanation: 서술자는 자신이 틀렸을지 모른다고 인정하며 'we can only act according to our kind'라고 말한다. 이어 '다르게 행동할 힘이 있었다면'으로 공식을 바꾸고 그런 힘이 없었음을 알았다고 밝힌다. 이는 자신의 한계를 받아들이는 체념의 태도이므로 B가 정답이다. 남을 탓하거나 과거 선택을 자랑하거나 미래를 기대하는 말은 없으므로 A, C, D는 틀리다.

The Suffolk (was it Surrey?) flirt
Without a pang threw over
Poor Jack and all his works like dirt,
And caught a richer lover.

We read one morning more to say
We had not been quite idle,
And then to end the arduous day
Enjoyed a swim in Rydal.

Next day the hundredweight of books
Was packed once more in cases,
We left the lakes and hills and brooks
And southward turned our faces.

Earnest, recording a period of intense and serious study

g.passage: Suppose thrown among us a person of well-developed intellect, but unacquainted with a single language or word that we use. It is absolutely useless to talk to him, because nothing that we say conveys any meaning to his mind. We can supply him no dictionary, because by hypothesis he knows no language to which we have access. How shall we proceed to communicate our ideas to him? Clearly there is but one possible way--namely, through his senses. Outside of this means of bringing him in contact with us we can have no communication with him. We, therefore, begin by showing him sensible objects, and letting him understand that certain words which we use correspond to those objects.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: Doubtful, suggesting that communication with the stranger may be impossible
Impatient, dismissing the stranger as unworthy of the effort involved
Amused, treating the stranger's confusion as a kind of harmless joke
Confident, reasoning step by step toward the one workable method

A boat-race, of course; and there must be a great show of previous practice, tremendous rivalry, and pressing competition, so that a strong feeling of partisanship would be aroused; while in truth, the race itself was to be a sham. g.passage: In fact, civilization from its very inception has been “machine-made.” It began when our remotest ancestor snatched the bough of a tree and decided thenceforth to walk erect, using the bough as staff and club--that is, as a machine. Every tool of every kind has been a machine; and the progress of the race has been determined by the number and efficiency of its machines, both those designed to compel peace and those designed to further the arts of peace. If you wish to measure the actual value of any civilization--value in producing healthy minds in healthy bodies--you need only inquire into the kind and number and efficiency of its machines. Why? Because the machine represents the effort of man to adjust himself to his environment, his environment to himself.
g.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To warn that modern machines threaten healthy minds and bodies
To describe how the earliest humans first learned to walk erect
To argue that tools designed for war have slowed human progress

g.passage:
When the second woman with the two little ones came up and begged for the toy, something hard and sullen and cruel rose in the widow's heart, and she refused angrily to give up the thing. She hated those two boys who had been spared when her own was taken. She would not make them happy.

"No, you shall not have it," she cried, clutching the Noah's ark fiercely. "I will destroy it."

The poor woman and the children followed her wistfully. The little boys were crying. They were cold and hungry and disappointed.
g.question: Based on the text, why does the widow refuse to give up the toy?
options: She resents that the boys were spared when her own son was taken.
She believes the toy is far too valuable to give away to strangers.
She hopes to sell the Noah's ark later to buy food for herself.
She fears the two boys will break the toy as soon as they get it.
g.explanation: 지문은 과부가 두 소년을 미워했다고 하며, 그 이유를 '자기 아이는 데려가졌는데 그들은 살아남았기 때문'이라고 밝힌다. 또 'She would not make them happy'라는 문장이 그 동기를 다시 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. 그녀는 장난감을 부수겠다고 했으므로 값이나 판매를 생각한 B, C는 틀리고, 소년들이 장난감을 망가뜨릴까 걱정하는 내용도 없어 D도 틀리다.

g.passage: For weeks it takes the edge off his bliss; for weeks he never glances at the addresses of his letters without a pang of dread; for weeks he never turns the handle of his door on his return home from his work without a shiver of apprehension. But not once does his eye alight on that feared handwriting; always his room is empty of that once so longed-for, and now dreaded presence. Ah, he is not so indispensable to her as he had fancied! She can do better without him than in his self-value had appeared possible. He need not be afraid that her fingers will ever again trace his name upon paper, or hurriedly lift his latch.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Joyful, celebrating a lover's long-awaited and happy reunion
Anxious, then rueful as the man's fear proves needless
Angry, condemning a woman for her cruelty toward the man
Calm, describing a man's untroubled and steady routine
g.explanation: 지문의 앞부분은 'pang of dread', 'shiver of apprehension'처럼 남자가 몇 주 동안 느끼는 불안을 반복해 보여 준다. 그러나 그 여인은 끝내 나타나지 않고, 'Ah, he is not so indispensable to her'에서 그는 자신이 생각만큼 중요하지 않았음을 씁쓸하게 깨닫는다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. 재회나 분노, 평온함은 지문에 드러나지 않으므로 A, C, D는 틀리다.

g.passage: There was so much truth in this that Mulrady checked a sigh as he gave the required permission, without saying that he had intended to remain. He could cook his own breakfast: he had done it before; and it would be something to occupy him. As to his dinner, perhaps he could go to the hotel at Rough-and-Ready. He worked on until the night had well advanced. Then, overcome with a certain restlessness that disturbed him, he was forced to put his books and papers away. It had begun to blow in fitful gusts, and occasionally the rain was driven softly across the panes like the passing of childish fingers. This disturbed him more than the monotony of silence, for he was not a nervous man.
g.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes Mulrady's relationship with the person who asked for permission?
options: He resents the person and is glad to be left alone at last.
He depends on the person for money and fears losing it.
He outranks the person yet quietly misses the person.
He barely knows the person and gives no thought to the request.
g.explanation: Mulrady는 '요청받은 허락'을 내주므로 상대보다 권한이 있는 위치에 있다. 그런데 그는 한숨을 참고, 자신이 남으려 했다는 말도 하지 않으며, 밤이 되자 침묵 속에서 불안을 느낀다. 이는 상대의 부재를 아쉬워함을 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. 혼자 남아 기뻐하거나 돈 문제를 걱정하거나 무관심한 모습은 없으므로 A, B, D는 틀리다.
